title: Designing with Classes
goal: In this lesson you will design a small program with a class that has data, __init__, and methods working together.
learn: Choose the attributes your thing needs
Use the objects in a tiny scene
idea: Here is a design tip. Pick a real thing, like a shop item, a pet, or a hero. List what it knows (attributes) and what it does (methods), and put the setup in __init__. Then create some objects and call their methods to tell a tiny story. That is designing with classes.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the starting stock to 6 and press Run. The first label should show x6.

practice.text: Design Book with title, pages in __init__, and a blurb method. Create one and call blurb.
practice.hint: __init__ should save title and pages on self. blurb prints something that uses self.title or self.pages.
practice.starterTip: self.title = title, self.pages = pages, and blurb: print(self.title, "has", self.pages, "pages").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if blurb uses attributes from __init__.

practice.text: Design Battery with percent in __init__ and use(n) that lowers percent. Demo one use.
practice.hint: In use, subtract n from self.percent. After b.use(20) on a Battery at 100, b.percent should be 80.
practice.starterTip: self.percent = self.percent - n inside use. The final print(b.percent) checks your work.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if percent becomes 80 after use(20).

quiz.question: When designing a class, what do you list first?

options.text: What it knows and what it does

quiz.correct: Right, a class design is data plus actions.
quiz.wrong: List what it knows and what it does.

quiz.question: Where should starting data be set?
quiz.correct: Yes, init builds a ready object.

quiz.question: What makes a tiny class scene?

options.text: Create objects and call their methods

quiz.correct: Right, objects acting out is what tells the story.

project.title: Tiny Shop
project.desc: Make an Item class with name, price, and stock, and with label and sell methods. Make two items, label both, sell from one, and label again.
